speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Government has considered complementing LUSH 3.0's focus on greenery provision with a biodiversity metric that measures net ecological gain or loss, similar to the UK’s Biodiversity Net Gain framework, so that developments are assessed not only by how green they appear but by whether they result in a measurable improvement in biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of National Development)
text: This supports biodiversity, enhances liveability and mitigates urban heat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of National Development)
text: Despite our land constraints, we are committed to enhancing biodiversity even as we undertake developments to meet different land use needs for our people, such as housing, education, healthcare, transport and jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of National Development)
text: For example, we are safeguarding more green spaces, establishing additional nature parks, restoring core habitats and conducting species recovery for rare, threatened and endemic species.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister of National Development)
text: These efforts work in tandem with LUSH to improve biodiversity in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: First, I thank the Minister of State for his reply.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My first supplementary question, will the Ministry of National Development (MND) consider complementing the green plot ratio with an indicator that reflects ecological value, such as the use of native species or support for urban wildlife, by mandating a native biodiversity score, so that our green spaces contribute to quality greenery and biodiversity to beyond visual amenity, and in the case of LUSH, to discourage ornamental plants with lower ecological value?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Has MND considered adopting a similar quantitative baseline in the interest of transparency and accountability?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I believe that with a measurable net-gain target, it can better assist MND to ensure that our City in Nature vision is maintaining or improving functional habitats over time.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My third supplementary question, the Ecological Profiling Exercise (EPE) identifies critical stepping stones for wildlife, but many LUSH-compliant developments remain isolated in green islands rather than contagious green linkages.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Has MND considered more explicitly aligning existing programmes, like LUSH, more directly to EPE-identified priority corridors, so that developments in these locations contribute to strengthening ecological connectivity beyond isolated green plots?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And we have discussed this multiple times, so thank you for working together with us first.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, I did some study last night and the UK developers have cited the BNG as costly and also imposing delays to building homes for UK citizens.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The UK government in itself has also proposed rollbacks to the BNG, because it is impacting their ability to build homes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Even the UK, with their larger land sizes, has difficulty building their homes and are reviewing this, so I think we need to exercise caution when thinking about applying that to our context.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And in that regard, I also wanted to take a larger holistic view on how we are safeguarding biodiversity.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is a holistic approach towards enhancing biodiversity, in addition to what we are doing with LUSH, which is a downstream measure, and it is in aim to build and incorporate livability into our urban spaces.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In that regard, I thought it is also being very, very helpful for us to give a concrete example about this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In Chencharu, Yishun, for example, we are balancing development together with biodiversity.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And this illustrates the point that I am trying to make.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And in that regard also, we have worked very closely with our nature groups and environmental efforts.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I also wanted to take this opportunity to also respond to Member He Ting Ru's point on Wednesday about our engagements with nature groups being one-sided.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That is not true, because we work with our nature groups very extensively.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I met with them even on Valentine's Day last month.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And I worked with Dr Shawn Lum, for example, on the Nature Society Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us squeeze in one more last Parliamentary Question.
